Both did the job — I added "Design" to the first two cards, it applied to both at once, reused my existing label instead of making a duplicate, and cleared the selection afterward. Good.

On the style, I prefer the **selection-mode version** — the one where I first tap "Select bookmarks." Most of the time I'm just reading and clicking through my list, and having a checkbox sitting on every card all the time feels busy for something I only do now and then when I'm tidying up. Deliberately entering a "now I'm selecting" mode keeps my everyday view calm and makes it clear when I'm about to act on a batch. So let's go with that. The action set on the bar — label, mark read, put away, delete — is a sensible bunch too.

Two related touches I'd want on this same bulk idea, since we're here:

- The actions should work both ways, to match what an individual card can do: if I can bulk-*mark read*, I'd also want to bulk-*mark unread*, and if I can bulk-*add* a label, I'd want to bulk-*remove* one too. Otherwise I can do a thing to many but have to undo it one at a time.
- When I've already narrowed my list — say I've filtered to a label or run a search — I'd sometimes want to apply an action to *everything* in that filtered view in one go, without ticking each card. So a quick "select all of these" that respects whatever filter I'm looking at.

The selection-and-batch-action mechanism you've shown is right; could we round it out with those reverse actions and the "apply to the whole filtered set" option?
